original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: Is there an unsearched width-neutral local move or packing improvement for the highest open claim (#1193/#1218 X54 mixed-T37, kappa 0.001675809683500501), rather than the selected #1094 packing?
scope_change_reason: The selected #1094 packing is superseded by open claims on the same lineage; the bounded residual question that matters is whether the strongest open construction still has local or packing headroom.
bottleneck_link: The complex supplier binds; on this line every recent gain came from width-neutral local moves or packing. This bounds both for the incumbent words/mix and prices the inventory changes that could still help.
stop_rule: Stop after exhaustive toolkit sweeps on both final words and an exact or ILP packing bound; build an admitted construction only if a gain appears.
evidence: evidence/sweeps (0 gains in 2x(2238+50+161) candidates), evidence/PACKING.json (exact Phi invariant and idle optimum), evidence/AGGREGATE.json (ILP = incumbent; dual prices). Superseded in part by #1274 (local gain outside the #1186 families) and #1252/#1268/#1280 (idle-axis repartition outside the bin-remainder model).
author: Wronskode
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude (Claude Code): search runs, analysis, code and text.

open_questions.question: Is there a single-helper entrance/end change whose local frame cost passes the width/Phi screening rule (e.g. 9->8 below 13.3 units, 4->5 below 86.9 per helper)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Packing and width-neutral moves are saturated for the incumbent; only a changed helper inventory or new local word can move kappa on this line.
open_questions.first_step: Price candidate single-helper interface changes with the #1186 Pricer and apply the README score; rerun aggregate.py with the new variant.
open_questions.blocked_by: No generator for single-helper interface changes; #1176 reports demotions need whole four-helper groups.

open_questions.question: How do the width/Phi shadow prices and the optimal demotion-group count change once idle rank-48 children can be repartitioned (48+48 -> 45+51, #1252/#1280)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Idle reshaping changes the marginal value of idle mass, hence lambda and the break-even of an entrance group; the 208-group mix may no longer be optimal.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun aggregate.py with an idle-cost function allowing empty capacity-48 bins to pair into 45+51 at the rate #1280 achieves.
open_questions.blocked_by: The achievable pairing rate depends on #1252's per-(replica, port) commuting-axis condition, which is not modelled here.
